name: Chapli Kabab
description: Pashtun-style chapli kababs made with seasoned beef mince, crushed coriander and cumin, herbs and tomato, shaped thin and shallow-fried until browned and cooked through.
ingredients: 750 g beef mince with some fat
1 medium tomato, finely chopped and excess juice removed
1 small onion, finely chopped and squeezed of excess moisture
1 tsp red chili flakes or to taste
method: Combine the beef mince with the squeezed onion, green chillies, fresh coriander, crushed coriander seeds, cumin, chilli flakes, maize flour, egg and salt. Mix until the seasonings are evenly distributed and the mince begins to hold together.
Fold in the finely chopped, well-drained tomato shortly before shaping; removing excess tomato and onion moisture helps prevent the mixture from becoming loose.
With damp hands, form broad, relatively thin patties of even thickness. If they feel too soft to handle cleanly, chill the shaped or mixed kababs briefly before frying.
Heat a shallow layer of oil over medium heat. Add the kababs in batches with space between them so the pan temperature does not drop sharply.
Let the first side develop a firm browned crust before turning. Cook the second side until browned and make sure the centre is fully cooked, using a reliable doneness check for minced meat.
Drain briefly so excess surface oil runs off, then serve hot with chutney, naan, sliced onion or salad.
tips: Remove excess moisture from onion and tomato to help the kababs hold together.
Make the patties relatively thin so the centre cooks before the exterior burns.
storage: Cool cooked kababs promptly and refrigerate covered. Reheat the portion you plan to eat until thoroughly hot.
